facts.text: Gateway's roots stretch back thousands of years, when Athabascan peoples like the Dena'ina and Ahtna hunted, fished, and traded along the Matanuska and Susitna rivers.
The landscape around Gateway rolls gently, with wetlands and low hills drained by streams such as Wasilla Creek, echoing the valley's glacial past.
Elevations in Gateway range from about 200 feet near the valley floor to roughly 1,000 feet on surrounding hills, creating diverse topography.
The Crevasse Moraine Trail System offers 6.7 miles of paths winding through glacial ridges, forested loops, and snowy slopes for year‑round hiking and snowshoeing.
Gateway experiences a subarctic climate, with long, cold winters and short, cool summers typical of the Dfc Köppen classification.
Named for its position, Gateway serves as a literal gateway to Alaska's rugged interior, bridging suburban life with wilderness adventures.
